title: GatewayConfiguration
description:
Root aggregate of the gateway configuration. Loaded from
config/current.json by the configuration manager (B2). Holds the
gateway-level settings plus the source, sink, and route definitions that
describe the data flow.

Sources.description:
Configured source connector instances. Default empty — a gateway
with no sources is technically valid (and is the starting state of
a freshly provisioned gateway).

Sinks.description: Configured sink connector instances. Default empty.

Routes.description:
Configured routes. Default empty. A route references one source by
SourceInstanceId and one or more sinks by
SinkInstanceIds; cross-record validation
(verifying those ids resolve) happens in B2.

GatewaySettings.description:
Gateway-level identity and host settings. This is the Gateway
section of the top-level configuration JSON. Per blueprint §10, the
gateway identity is established at first start and persisted; this record
holds the configurable subset of that identity plus host-process settings.

GatewayName.description: Human-readable gateway name shown in the admin UI.

Site.description:
Customer site or location label. Optional but recommended for fleet
management.

LicenseFile.description:
Path to the license file relative to the gateway data directory.
Default "license.json".

LogLevel.description:
Minimum log level. One of Trace, Debug, Information,
Warning, Error, Critical, None. Default
Information. Stored as a string to avoid a Core dependency on
Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions; the host project
parses this into the appropriate log level type.

DataPath.description:
Filesystem path (relative or absolute) to the gateway's persistent
data directory. Holds buffers, drafts, history, audit logs, and the
identity file. Default "data/".

HealthCheckPort.description:
TCP port for the lightweight HTTP health check endpoint
(GET /health). Default 8080 per blueprint §8.1 sample.

ManagementApiSettings.description:
Configuration for the local REST management API exposed by the gateway.
The API itself lands in Phase 4; this record is the JSON-loadable shape
only and is consumed by the host project when it stands the API up.

Enabled.description: True if the management API is enabled. Default true.

Port.description: TCP port the API listens on. Default 8443 per blueprint §8.1 sample.

RequireAuth.description:
True if the API requires authentication. Default true — the
management API exposes config and license operations and should not
be unauthenticated in any production deployment.

TlsCertPath.description:
Filesystem path to the TLS certificate (PFX) used by the API
listener. Optional; if absent, the host falls back to plain HTTP
(intended for development only).

Enabled.description:
True if the watchdog is enabled. Default true per blueprint
§11 reliability requirements.

RestartOnFailure.description:
True if the host should restart on unrecoverable failure. Default
true per blueprint §8.1 sample.

SourceInstanceConfig.description:
JSON DTO for a single source connector instance — one configured use of
a protocol module against one physical device. Distinct from the runtime
SourceConfiguration which adapter implementations
receive after Core has loaded and validated the JSON.

InstanceId.description:
Stable identifier for this source connector instance (e.g.,
"focas-jyoti17"). Lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must
start with a letter or digit.

ProtocolName.description:
Protocol module name (e.g., "focas2", "mtlinki",
"modbus"). Lowercase, must match the adapter's declared
ProtocolName.

Enabled.description: True if this instance is enabled in the running gateway. Default true.

DeviceId.description:
Identifier of the physical device behind this source (e.g.,
"Jyoti17CNC").

Connection.description:
Protocol-specific connection block. Held opaquely as JsonElement
because the schema differs per protocol (FOCAS2 has IpAddress+Port,
Modbus has UnitId, MQTT has BrokerHost+ClientId, etc.). The protocol
adapter is responsible for parsing this into its own typed connection
record during InitializeAsync.

Polling.description:
Polling parameters. Optional; defaults supplied by
PollingSettings when omitted.

Tags.description:
Free-form tags attached to this instance for filtering and routing.
Default empty.

PollingSettings.description:
Polling parameters for a source connector instance. Used by the routing
engine (Phase 1 C3) to drive periodic PollAsync
calls.

IntervalMs.description:
Polling interval in milliseconds. Default 1000 ms per blueprint §8.1 sample.
Adapters may impose protocol-specific minimums (see §18.6) — for example,
FOCAS2 should not be polled faster than ~3-5 seconds in production.

MaxConsecutiveErrors.description:
Number of consecutive polling failures after which the source is
auto-disabled and marked Failed.
Default 3 per blueprint §8.1 sample. 0 disables the auto-disable.

SinkInstanceConfig.description:
JSON DTO for a single sink connector instance — one configured use of a
sink protocol module against one destination. Distinct from the runtime
SinkConfiguration which adapter implementations
receive after Core has loaded and validated the JSON.

InstanceId.description:
Stable identifier for this sink connector instance (e.g.,
"mqtt-eremos-main").

ProtocolName.description:
Protocol module name (e.g., "mqtt", "http", "tcp",
"opcua-server"). Must match the adapter's declared
ProtocolName.

Enabled.description: True if this instance is enabled in the running gateway. Default true.

Connection.description:
Protocol-specific connection block. Held opaquely as JsonElement
— the sink adapter parses it during initialisation.

Publishing.description:
Publishing parameters. Universal fields are typed; protocol-specific
extras (MQTT topic prefix, HTTP headers, etc.) are preserved in
Extras via JsonExtensionDataAttribute.

PublishingSettings.description:
Publishing parameters common to all sink connector instances. Universal
fields (batch size, batch interval) are typed and validated by Core.
Protocol-specific publishing knobs (e.g., MQTT QoS, HTTP headers) are
captured in Extras via JsonExtensionDataAttribute
and parsed by the sink adapter when it initialises.

BatchSize.description: Target batch size for published messages. Default 100 per blueprint §8.1 sample.

BatchIntervalMs.description:
Maximum time to wait before flushing a partial batch, in milliseconds.
Default 250 ms per blueprint §8.1 sample.

RouteConfig.description:
JSON DTO for a single route — a named data flow from one source to one
or more sinks, optionally with transforms and a buffer policy.

Name.description: Human-readable name for the route, shown in the admin UI.

SourceInstanceId.description:
InstanceId of the source feeding
this route. Validation that this id resolves to a real configured
source happens in B2 (cross-record validation).

Filter.description: Tag include / exclude filter. Default includes everything per blueprint §4.4.

Transforms.description:
Optional transform pipeline configuration. When null, the route is
identity (points pass through unchanged after filtering).

SinkInstanceIds.description:
One or more sink instance ids that receive points from this route.
Per blueprint §3 design principles, a single source can fan out to
many sinks via a single route. The list must be non-empty; B2's
validator enforces the non-empty constraint at apply time.

Buffer.description:
Per-route buffer policy. Default supplies sensible production values
(StoreAndForward, 10k depth, 7 day retention, drop oldest on overflow).

Delivery.description:
Per-route delivery policy. Default is AtLeastOnce with 5 retries and
parallel fanout.

Enabled.description: True if this route is enabled in the running gateway. Default true.

TagFilterConfig.description:
Include / exclude glob patterns deciding which tags from the source flow
through the route. Per blueprint §4.4, the default Include
is ["*"] — when no filter is specified, every tag from the source
passes through.

Include.description:
Glob patterns of tags to include. Default ["*"] per blueprint §4.4
— every tag from the source is included unless overridden.

Exclude.description:
Glob patterns of tags to exclude. Applied after Include.
Optional; null means no exclusions.

TransformProfileConfig.description:
Configuration for the transform pipeline applied by a route. All sub-blocks
are optional; an entirely null transform profile means the route is identity
(points pass through unchanged).

TagMapping.description:
Source-tag-name → canonical-tag-name mapping. Applied first in the
pipeline. Tags not in this map pass through with their original name.

Deadband.description:
Per-tag absolute deadband threshold. The routing engine suppresses
subsequent readings of a tag whose value has not changed by at least
the threshold. Interpreted as an absolute change in the numeric value.
A tag may not appear in both Deadband and
DeadbandPercent; cross-record validation enforces this.

DeadbandPercent.description:
Per-tag percentage deadband threshold, expressed as a fraction in
(0, 1] (e.g., 0.05 = 5%). The step passes a new reading
only when |current - last| / max(|last|, epsilon) ≥ threshold.
A tag may not appear in both Deadband and this map.

RateLimitMs.description:
Per-tag minimum interval (in milliseconds) between published values.
Used to cap publish frequency on noisy or high-rate tags. Values must
be strictly positive; cross-record validation enforces this.

EnrichmentTags.description:
Static metadata to attach to every point flowing through the route
(e.g., site, line, shift). In C1 this field is intentionally dormant:
it is accepted, validated, and persisted by the configuration subsystem,
but the transform pipeline does not yet include an enrichment step.
A later milestone (C1.5 or C3) will activate it. Until then, values in
this map have no runtime effect.

BufferPolicyConfig.description:
Per-route buffer policy controlling buffering mode, capacity, retention,
and overflow behaviour. Per blueprint §4.4 and §6, every route has its own
buffer policy; per-route storage is per-blueprint §19.3 with per-sink
cursors.

Mode.description:
Buffering mode for the route. Default StoreAndForward
— production routes are durable by default per blueprint §6.

MaxDepth.description:
Maximum number of points the buffer holds before OnOverflow
applies. Default 10,000 per blueprint §8.1 sample. 0 disables the depth cap.

MaxAgeDays.description:
Maximum age in days for buffered points. Older points are evicted.
Default 7 days per blueprint §8.1 sample. 0 disables the age cap.

OnOverflow.description:
Behaviour when the buffer hits its capacity ceiling. Default
DropOldest — preserves freshness.

BufferMode.description:
Buffering mode for a route. Locked at config-load time per
blueprint §4.4 and §6.

DropPolicy.description:
What the routing engine does when a route buffer hits its capacity ceiling.
Per blueprint §19.8, sources are never blocked by sinks; the buffer absorbs
the mismatch and the drop policy decides what happens at the ceiling.

DeliveryPolicyConfig.description:
Per-route delivery policy. Controls delivery semantics, retry / backoff
behavior, and fanout parallelism. Used by the C3 routing engine to drive
SinkPublisher retry state machines and the
FanoutDispatcher.

Mode.description:
Delivery semantic for the route. Default
AtLeastOnce per blueprint §19.7.
AtMostOnce requires
None (cross-record rule 7).
ExactlyOnce is intentionally NOT a member of
DeliveryMode per blueprint §19.7 — not supported in v1.
The rejection is enforced at the enum level (a pinned B1 test
asserts the absence of an ExactlyOnce member); no validator
rule is required.

MaxRetries.description:
Maximum number of retry attempts per failed batch before the sink is
marked Degraded per blueprint §19.4. Default 5. Set to 0 to
disable retry (the sink degrades on the first failure).

InitialBackoffMs.description:
Initial retry backoff in milliseconds. The retry state machine
applies exponential backoff starting from this value, capped at
MaxBackoffMs and randomized by JitterPercent.
Default 100 ms.

MaxBackoffMs.description:
Cap on the exponential backoff curve in milliseconds. The backoff
will not exceed this value regardless of attempt count. Must be
greater than or equal to InitialBackoffMs (cross-record
rule 12). Default 30,000 ms (30 seconds).

BackoffMultiplier.description:
Multiplier applied to the previous backoff to compute the next one.
Standard exponential backoff uses 2.0. Must be at least 1.0. Default 2.0.

JitterPercent.description:
Randomized jitter applied to each backoff interval, expressed as a
percentage of the computed backoff. A value of 10 means the actual
delay is uniform in [backoff × 0.9, backoff × 1.1]. Default 10.

FanoutParallel.description:
True if the routing engine should publish to fanout sinks in parallel
rather than sequentially. Default true. Per blueprint §19.2,
fanout is independent per sink regardless of this flag — this controls
only whether the dispatch happens concurrently or one-after-another.

DeliveryMode.description:
Delivery semantic for a route. Only the two modes supported in v1 per
blueprint §19.7 are present.
